ev.notes:
Expected percent return by horizon (1-40y): our strategy vs total VC market vs the best 10 VCs.

Annual rates (net to investor) and where each comes from:
  MARKET   10.0%/yr (range 7-13). Cambridge Associates US VC index, pooled net IRR to Dec 2025:
           20y 12.9%, 25y 8.1%, 10y 14.9%; post-2000 VC PME ~0.94-0.96 (Harris-Jenkinson-Kaplan),
           i.e. roughly public-equity returns going forward.
  STRATEGY (updated round 4, SEC Form D 2010-2021, 25k startups) market + 1.5 pt (range -1..+4):
           "best quality in the cheaper half of first raises" beat owning every first raise by +37%
           on the sealed 2018-21 holdout ($5M floor; +45% at $3M, +27% at $8M) and +40..+90% on
           2015-17. Paper markups over 4.5 years, not cash: halved, spread over a 10-year fund.
  (round 3) market + 0.5 pt (range -2..+2): the drop-bottom-third rule scored
           +26% on 2008-10 but only +6.5% (CI -34..+28) on the sealed 2012 lockbox; the lockbox wins.
           (Round-2 text follows.) market + 1.0 pt (range -1..+3). Broad index of every accessible seed/A deal (or 20+ funds)
           across >=5 vintages, minus the model's bottom third. Screen measured +21% (2008-10) and
           +19% (2011, second look) over a ~10y life ~= +2 pt/yr, halved for shrinkage/frictions.
           Emerging/prior-top-quartile manager tilt (HJKS PME 1.24/1.20 vs ~0.96) adds ~+0.5, an
           extra fee layer costs ~-0.5: net +1.0.
  TOP 10   HINDSIGHT, NOT INVESTABLE. Years 1-10: 31%/yr = mean top-decile net IRR of 2007-2014
           vintages (PitchBook 2Q18). Beyond 10y no fund stays top decile; the best long records in
           public LP disclosures are ~17-22%/yr (Sequoia legacy 17.4%, Khosla IV 22%), so 20%/yr after year 10.
EV = mean outcome ((1+r)^T - 1). Median uses 25%/yr volatility for a diversified VC book.

gp.assumptions:
Fund economics: % return on the manager's (GP's) own money vs an outside investor (LP) in
the same fund. Percent only.

Fund: 10-year life, management fee 2%/yr of commitments years 1-5 and 1.5% years 6-10 (17.5% of
commitments in total; that's money not invested), carry 20% of profits above returned capital, no
hurdle (standard in VC). GP commits 2% of the fund alongside LPs and pays no fee/carry on it.
Fee income minus operating costs is shown separately (costs = 70% of fees for a small fund).
Gross multiple = what the invested capital returns; LP net follows from it.

Gross scenarios (multiple on invested capital over ~10y), sourced:
  market: LP net 10%/yr over a ~7y average hold ~ net TVPI 1.95x -> gross ~2.65x
  our rule: market +6.5% (2012 lockbox point estimate for the drop-bottom-third rule)
  top quartile fund: net TVPI ~2.5x (CA/PitchBook 2007-2014 vintages) -> gross ~3.2x
  top decile: net ~3.0x -> gross ~3.9x
  bad: gross 1.0x (money back before fees)

jcurve.assumptions:
Horizon returns that respect HOW venture money moves: Takahashi-Alexander (Yale) fund cash-flow
model with fees, carry and the J-curve, run as a program that starts with $1 today.

Mechanics (yearly):
  * You set aside 100. Uncalled cash earns CASH_RATE (3.5%).
  * Each fund calls capital: 25% / 33% / 50%-of-remaining in years 1/2/3+ (TA defaults).
  * Fees 2%/yr of commitment years 1-5, 1.5% years 6-10, paid out of called capital.
  * Invested NAV grows at gross rate G. Distributions = NAV*(1+G)*(age/LIFE)^BOW, LIFE=12, BOW=2.5.
  * 20% carry on distributions once a fund has returned its paid-in capital.
  * Every distribution is recommitted to a new fund the next year (a perpetual VC programme).
  G is solved so that a single fund's NET IRR equals the target:
      market 10%  (CA US VC index, 20y 12.9% / 25y 8.1%)
      strategy  round 5: quality-in-cheap-half edge pooled over 3 out-of-sample windows (+50%),
                halved to +25% on the fund multiple, held through a low-fee vehicle (1%/10%)
                -> net IRR from analysis/edge.py (~16.7%); via a standard 2/20 fund it is ~14.2%
      best-10 hindsight: 31% for fund 1 (top-decile vintages 2007-14), 20% for later funds.
Value at horizon T = cash + NAV of all funds; percent = value - 100.
